comparison_with_bh1_bh2.observation: Historic fill bases are 1.10 m in BH1, 0.60 m in BH2 and 1.30 m in BH3, a local range of 0.60 to 1.30 m below each hole's logged ground. BH3's fill description does not mention brick; its absence from the description is not proof of absence.

Sandstone tops are 6.50 m in BH1, 5.50 m in BH2 and 6.40 m in BH3; all three logs end at 8.10 m. These are local depths with no verified common surveyed datum, not an established bedrock surface at the demonstration point.

BH3 has granular material directly below fill, unlike the upper clay/clayey-sand sequence in BH1 and upper sandy clay in BH2. BH3 also logs a clay layer at 3.90 to 4.30 m and clayey fine sand at 5.00 to 5.30 m. The logs support testing variability, not assuming cross-hole continuity.
All three record dry drilling with added water and chiselling in the deeper cemented material. None supplies a present groundwater regime, measured rock-quality basis or design parameters.

conditional_gi_implications.inference: Where these records prove relevant to the actual works, target fill-base variability, local clay and granular lenses, the weathered/cemented sand-to-sandstone transition and obstruction/advancement requirements. Final locations, quantities and depths require the site footprint and engineering influence zone.

Obtain appropriate groundwater monitoring and test-quality information; use suitable coring and laboratory testing if rock behaviour controls the design. Do not derive bearing capacity, strength, stiffness or dewatering rates from these historic notes.

duplicate_coverage.page_3: All three repeat the September 1988 exploratory-hole location plan, contract 1829, drawing 2, showing BH1-BH3 and TP1-TP6 and the historical proposed-building outline.
duplicate_coverage.page_4: All three repeat the September 1988 west-east geological section, contract 1829, drawing 3, containing questioned correlations and a warning that ground levels were extrapolated from another drawing.
duplicate_coverage.counting_rule: Count TP1, TP2 and TP3 once each. Count the three shared drawings once as report-family context; they are also present in the previously reviewed Edgbaston PDFs.

depth_units.interpreted_units: m below the pit's recorded ground surface
depth_units.qualification: Page 1 uses decimal depth intervals without an explicit adjacent unit label. Metres are interpreted from the investigation context and the shared metric geological section; no surveyed pit datum is provided on the combined sheet.
depth_units.confidence: high for numerical transcription; contextual interpretation for metric units

shared_context_limits.note: The historic plans establish report-family context, not the current site boundary or present positions/levels without georeferencing.

Questioned connections and extrapolated ground levels do not confirm continuous strata or surveyed elevations. Do not turn the interpreted boulder-clay key into an independently established formation for every pit.
Borehole SPT entries shown in the shared section belong to boreholes, not to the trial pits. No SPT results are assigned to TP1-TP3.
No quantitative design strength, stiffness, bearing resistance, permeability, groundwater regime or current excavation stability is established for the proposed works.

TP4-TP6.review_scope: Complete visual review of all 12 pages in SP08SE128, SP08SE129 and SP08SE130. Derived factual paraphrases only; no original scans, personal names, signatures or contact details are reproduced.

duplicate_coverage.assessment: Each four-page PDF contains the same shared TP4-TP6 log sheet at page 1 and the same three drawings at pages 2-4. The BGS wrappers identify different records and grid positions. There are three distinct trial-pit records, not nine independent pit logs.
duplicate_coverage.verification: Corresponding embedded original scan images have identical SHA-256 hashes across all three PDFs, supplementing visual inspection of every page.

shared_drawing_context.project: Lucas Institute Annexe, University of Birmingham; ground investigation; contract 1829.
shared_drawing_context.date_limit: The drawing date is not a stated excavation date for any of TP4-TP6. The shared pit sheet has no excavation date.

pages.content: Historic exploratory-hole location plan showing BH1-BH3 and TP1-TP6, a proposed building outline, an approximately 1 m retaining wall and vegetation.
Interpreted west-east geological section; questioned correlations, groundwater-level key and borehole SPT entries. Ground levels are stated to be extrapolated from another drawing.

limits: Drawings are historic context, not a current site survey or proof that the original proposal was built as shown.
Do not assign borehole SPT entries on the shared section to the trial pits.
Section correlations and the boulder-clay interpretation do not replace the individual pit lithological descriptions.
Extrapolated section levels must not be adopted as surveyed pit or development-site datums.

units_and_datum.qualification: The pit sheet prints decimal depth values without an explicit depth-unit heading. Metres are the contextual interpretation supported by the associated metric investigation drawings and depth scale; the page explicitly labels only the paving-slab dimensions in feet. Retain this qualification if strict original-unit verification is required.
units_and_datum.datum: Intervals are nominal depths from each original pit's zero, conventionally interpreted as logged ground. No independently surveyed pit ground-level elevation or present-day surface datum is supplied. The intervals_m_bgl schema does not certify the reference level.
units_and_datum.confidence: High for the printed decimal values; metric unit interpretation is contextual; surveyed datum unavailable.
units_and_datum.sample_code_note: The TP sheets record D without defining the code. Disturbed is a conventional interpretation, not an explicit legend on these sheets.

closed_acquisition_gap: Original records for Edgbaston BH3 and TP1-TP6 retrieved and reviewed. This does not close narrative report, laboratory-results, survey-datum, site-relevance or groundwater gaps.
new_priority: Locate and assess the historical TP4 bathing-pool feature with ash/debris fill, pungent water and excavation collapse. Develop environmental linkages and safe GI/temporary-works response where relevant to the actual works; no contaminant identity or current condition is established.

prior_d02_shared_context.status: historical D02 context; missing-log acquisition statements superseded by D03

content.review_scope: Visual review of all four pages of each original BGS PDF; factual paraphrases for a preliminary desk study, without design parameters.

shared_pages.description: Same historical site-location plans in both PDFs, with different BGS wrappers. Drawing 1, contract 1829, September 1988.

Same exploratory-hole location plan in both PDFs. Drawing 2, September 1988; shows BH1, BH2, BH3 and TP1 to TP6, a historical proposed-building footprint, an approximately 1 m retaining wall and vegetation. This is a historical plan, not a current site boundary.

Same west-to-east geological section in both PDFs. Drawing 3, September 1988; depicts BH1 to BH3 and trial pits with questioned correlations. It explicitly states that ground levels were extrapolated from another drawing. The interpreted boulder-clay key does not turn the individual logs' sandy-clay descriptions into a confirmed site-wide till unit. Do not infer current groundwater or a surveyed borehole datum from this section.

report_family_gap.note: The shared exploratory plan and section show BH3 and TP1 to TP6 in addition to the two individual logs reviewed here. Obtain the complete investigation report and remaining original logs before finalising the ground model or GI scope; no detailed findings for those additional holes have been transcribed from these diagrams.

conditional_gi_implications.inference: Reconcile the drilling-date discrepancy and georeference the historical plan to the actual development before transferring any depths or observations.

If relevant to the actual site and works, target made-ground thickness, shallow soft pockets, clay/granular variability and the sand-to-weak-sandstone transition. The two historical fill bases are 1.10 and 0.60 m, and sandstone tops 6.50 and 5.50 m; these are observations at those holes only.
Select investigation equipment for cobbles and weak rock; consider coring where rock quality affects design. Chiselling and short penetration seating blows do not establish competent bearing rock.
Obtain appropriately screened and surveyed groundwater monitoring with repeat observations where relevant to the works. Historic dry drilling notes do not justify omitting groundwater assessment.
